question.question:
An amortizing bond is issued with face value USD 5000. Principal is repaid in three installments at the ends of years 1, 2 and 3: 25 percent of face at year 1, 35 percent of face at year 2, and the remaining balance at year 3. Each year-end coupon equals the coupon rate times the principal outstanding during that year. The year-1 coupon rate is 5 percent; the rate changes by 100 basis points at the start of year 2 and by a further 100 basis points at the start of year 3 (negative means a cut). The issuer may call the bond at the end of year 2, immediately after the year-2 coupon and installment are paid, by paying 102 percent of the principal still outstanding. Assume the issuer calls only if that call payment is strictly less than the present value, at the end of year 2, of the year-3 coupon plus final principal discounted one year at the effective annual yield of 2.5 percent. An investor settles 90 days after issue and uses a 360-day year, so a year-k cash flow is discounted by (1+y)^(k - days/360) with the same yield y. Compute the investor's dirty price at settlement: the present value of all cash flows actually received, namely the year-1 and year-2 scheduled payments, then the call payment if the bond is called or the year-3 payment otherwise.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Principal still outstanding after the year-2 installment.
Value at end of year 2 of the year-3 coupon plus final principal.
Whether the issuer calls at the end of year 2.
Total cash the investor receives at the end of year 2.
